title: Newborns already prefer faces, in a textbook summary
summary: OpenStax says vision is a newborn's least developed sense, and that newborns already show a preference for faces.
body: OpenStax Psychology says a newborn's senses are significant but not fully developed, and that vision is the least developed sense. Even so, the page says newborns already show a preference for faces, and that many inborn preferences support interaction with caregivers. This card is that textbook sentence. A separate laboratory paper, opened on its own, tests when an upright face-like pattern actually draws longer looking. The textbook line does not state the age in hours or the contrast conditions of that paper.

sources.title: 9.3 Stages of Development
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: Supports the sentence that newborns already show a preference for faces, in the infancy sensory paragraph. OpenStax Psychology, first edition (publish date 2014-12-08), CC BY 4.0. Paraphrase of the opened page; the cited primary paper was not opened.
